title: Faster quantum linear system solver beyond the condition number
authors: Alexander M. Dalzell, Jianqiang Li, Yuan Su
abstract: The spectral condition number is a widely adopted measure of worst-case cost for quantum linear system solvers. Yet it can significantly overestimate the actual runtime for a typical problem instance. We present two quantum algorithms that produce the normalized solution $|x\rangle$ of linear system $Ax=| b \rangle$ to accuracy $ε$ with complexity independent of the condition number $κ=\lVert A^{-1}\rVert$. We focus on the standard input model where $A$ is accessed through a block encoding and $| b \rangle$ is prepared by a unitary. But we also introduce an affine dilation model that encodes $A$ and $| b \rangle$ jointly, allowing further refinements of the query complexity. Our truncation-based solver makes an optimal number of queries to $| b \rangle$ and $\operatorname{\mathbf{O}}\left(κ_{\mathrm{eff}}\operatorname{polylog}\left(\frac{κ_{\mathrm{eff}}}ε\right)\right)$ queries to $A$. We prove a family of upper bounds on the effective condition number, including $κ_{\mathrm{eff}}\leq\frac{\lVert(A^\dagger A)^{-t/2}|x\rangle\rVert^{1/t}}{ε^{1/t}}$ for positive even integer $t$ and $κ_{\mathrm{eff}}\leq\frac{\lVert A^{-1\dagger}(A^\dagger A)^{-(t-1)/2}|x\rangle\rVert^{1/t}}{ε^{1/t}}$ for positive odd $t$, overcoming the $κ$-barrier. Our filtering-based solver is extremely simple with a favorable runtime prefactor. In particular, the solver has query complexity $6\frac{\lVert A^{-1\dagger}|x\rangle\rVert}ε\ln\left(\frac{1}ε\right)$ to leading order when the solution norm is known. We then present a similarly simple solution norm estimator with the same asymptotic cost up to logarithmic factors. Our quantum linear system solvers thus substantially improve a recent algorithm of Li, enabling faster quantum linear system solving beyond the condition number.
summary: This paper introduces two novel quantum algorithms designed to solve the linear system $Ax=|bangle$ with computational complexity that bypasses the limitations imposed by the spectral condition number $\kappa$. By introducing and utilizing an 'effective condition number' ($\kappa_{	ext{eff}}$), the solvers achieve significantly faster query scaling, representing a major algorithmic improvement for quantum simulation applications.
main_problem: The primary goal is developing quantum algorithms to solve linear systems of equations, $Ax=|bangle$, that achieve a computational complexity independent of the spectral condition number $\kappa$.
main_result: Two new solvers—one truncation-based and one filtering-based—are presented, achieving query complexities that scale with an 'effective condition number' ($\kappa_{	ext{eff}}$) or vector norms, thereby overcoming the traditional $\kappa$-barrier.
method: The authors introduce advanced quantum techniques involving effective truncation of the linear system and eigenstate filtering over the unit circle. They derive rigorous upper bounds for $\kappa_{	ext{eff}}$ to quantify this improved scaling.
model_or_system: The problem is framed within quantum computation models, analyzed under two input representations: the standard block encoding model and a more general affine dilation model that jointly encodes $A$ and $|bangle$.
key_observables: Effective condition number ($\kappa_{	ext{eff}}$), solution vector norm ($\|x\|$ ), and the required computational query complexity.
important_parameters: Target accuracy $\epsilon$, spectral condition number $\kappa$, and various derived parameters like $\alpha$ used in truncation bounds.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on defining and bounding $\kappa_{	ext{eff}}$ through specific mathematical transformations of the singular values, and assumes availability of relative approximations for the solution norm $\|x\|$ to achieve optimal scaling.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the concept of $\kappa_{	ext{eff}}$ using cumulative distribution weights; Table 1 compares the query complexities of various quantum solvers against this new work.
paper_structure: The paper reviews existing solvers dependent on $\kappa$, introduces the concept and bounds for $\kappa_{	ext{eff}}$, details two novel algorithms (truncation-based and filtering-based), proves their complexity improvements, and concludes by comparing them to prior state-of-the-art methods.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental algorithmic advances in quantum linear algebra, which is a core subroutine for many physical simulations (e.g., solving Hamiltonians or finding ground states) relevant to AMO physics and condensed matter theory.
